title: A New Era of Agentic Financial Operations Takes Shape at BeyondTheBlack 2026
summary: Explore how BlackLine’s Agentic Financial Operations Platform and Verity AI are shaping the future of finance with trusted, governed AI digital workforces.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


-


A Governed Digital Workforce: The next era of finance shifts from isolated task automation to a connected, governed workforce of intelligent AI agents operating side-by-side with finance teams.


-


Trust Through Four Layers: Successful agentic financial operations require a foundation of unified data, agentic orchestration, purpose-built solutions, and a centralized control console for strict governance.


-


Unified Record-to-Report & Invoice-to-Cash: Integrating financial close with AI-native consolidation and connecting the full Invoice-to-Cash lifecycle reduces manual exceptions and accelerates cash flow.


## From Insight to Action: Unveiling the Future of Governed Finance


What does the future of finance look like when AI agents can do more than assist with individual tasks? And what governance is required for finance teams to trust the numbers those agents produce? Our Innovation Keynote at BeyondTheBlack 2026 explored these central questions.


As organizations move from AI experimentation toward enterprise adoption, finance leaders face a fundamental challenge: unlocking the potential of intelligent agents without compromising the accuracy and control that financial operations demand. After all, if finance teams must manually verify every AI-generated result, much of the potential value of AI is lost. At BeyondTheBlack, we demonstrated how BlackLine is helping organizations address that challenge through our Agentic Financial Operations Platform, powered by Verity™ AI.


The innovations we unveiled span[platform architecture](https://www.blackline.com/platform/) ,[Record-to-Report](https://www.blackline.com/record-to-report/)


(R2R), and[Invoice-to-Cash](https://www.blackline.com/products/invoice-to-cash/)


(I2C). Together, they move beyond isolated automation toward a more connected model of financial operations—one where AI agents and finance professionals work side by side to execute processes and resolve exceptions. The opportunity extends beyond operational efficiency. When financial information is more accessible and trustworthy, organizations can make faster decisions and respond sooner to business opportunities.


Here are the biggest highlights from the keynote and what they mean for the Office of the CFO.


## A Platform Built for a Digital Workforce in Finance


For years, finance transformation has focused on automating individual activities, from[transaction matching](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/transaction-matching/) and[reconciliations](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/account-reconciliations/) to[journal entries](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/journals/) and collections. Those investments have helped organizations improve efficiency and strengthen financial controls, but they represent only part of the opportunity. The next evolution is connecting those activities so work can move intelligently across processes and teams. That connection brings faster access to financial information and deeper insights.


Imagine a[financial close](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/)


where agents retrieve supporting information and evaluate reconciliation quality. They prepare work for review and coordinate next steps based on established policies—all without finance professionals needing to initiate every action. That’s the direction BlackLine is advancing with its[Agentic Financial Operations Platform](https://www.blackline.com/products/verity-ai/) . During the keynote, we demonstrated how a digital workforce can operate across financial processes, with AI agents helping execute the work. Finance professionals remain responsible for oversight and judgment.


[Agentic financial operations](https://www.blackline.com/agentic-financial-operations/)


fundamentally transform how financial work is coordinated and governed, establishing an entirely different foundation for the Office of the CFO.


## Four Layers That Make Agentic Financial Operations Possible


A digital workforce for finance needs more than intelligent agents. It needs trusted financial data and the ability to execute financial processes. It also needs the governance required to operate with confidence. That’s why the[BlackLine Platform](https://www.blackline.com/platform/) brings together four foundational layers, each addressing a critical requirement for agentic financial operations.


1.


**Unified Data Foundation: Connecting the Financial Environment**


Financial data rarely lives in one place. It’s spread across ERPs, subledgers, and other enterprise systems. This fragmentation creates manual work that slows the path from information to insight and action. The Unified Data Foundation connects data and workflows across this environment. It gives agents the context and connectivity they need to perform meaningful financial work.


With Verity™ Integrate, BlackLine simplifies how organizations establish these connections through AI-powered integration capabilities. For finance teams, this eliminates the manual burden of extracting and preparing data across systems, allowing accountants to transition from transactional processors to strategic analysts. It also creates a stronger foundation for intelligent execution and more timely decisions.


2.


**Agentic Solutions: Where Financial Work Gets Done**


Intelligence and orchestration only create value when they can act on real financial processes. Purpose-built solutions from BlackLine provide the financial capabilities that agents can deploy across Record-to-Report and Invoice-to-Cash. These applications combine deep financial expertise from BlackLine with established workflows and embedded controls. They extend agentic execution into the everyday activities finance teams already manage.


3.


**Finance Control Console: Governing the Digital Workforce**


As organizations introduce more agents into financial operations, a new question emerges: How do finance leaders maintain visibility and accountability over work increasingly performed by AI? The Finance Control Console addresses that challenge with a centralized layer for governance and observability. It monitors agent activity, enforces policies, and maintains a full audit trail. Coverage extends beyond BlackLine-native agents to partner and customer-developed agents, as well as third-party agents operating within the governed environment.


For the Office of the CFO, this is essential. The value of AI depends on finance leaders trusting the numbers it produces. That means understanding what happened and why, and knowing who remains accountable. Together, these four layers provide the foundation for moving from isolated AI capabilities to coordinated, governed agentic financial operations.


4.


**Opening the Platform to a Broader Ecosystem of Agents**


A digital workforce won’t operate exclusively within one vendor’s technology. Finance organizations already rely on complex enterprise environments, and the next generation of AI will need to work across those investments. At BeyondTheBlack, we highlighted how BlackLine is extending the reach of its platform through agent-ready connectivity and open technologies.


With support for the open-standard Model Context Protocol (MCP), external AI agents and applications can securely interact with financial capabilities from BlackLine through an open, interoperable architecture. This lets organizations bring BlackLine financial expertise and trust infrastructure into broader agentic workflows. We also introduced an open source initiative that enables developers, partners, and customers to build and extend agentic capabilities.


The broader implication is clear: Organizations shouldn’t have to choose between adopting new AI technologies and preserving the financial controls and systems they already depend on. BlackLine is helping bring those worlds together, enabling finance teams to unlock the value of AI across their existing technology environments.


## Reimagining the Close: From Manual Activities to Intelligent Execution


One of the most significant opportunities for[agentic AI](https://www.blackline.com/record-to-report/agentic-ai/) lies in[Record-to-Report](https://www.blackline.com/record-to-report/) . The financial close combines many moving parts, from data preparation and reconciliation to consolidation and review. While individual activities have become increasingly automated, teams still spend considerable time coordinating work and investigating exceptions. They also lose hours moving information between systems. At BeyondTheBlack, we highlighted several innovations designed to address these challenges.


## Bringing Financial Close and Consolidation Together


With the general availability of[Financial Consolidation](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/consolidation/) , BlackLine is taking an AI-native, connected approach to two processes that have traditionally operated separately. Rather than treating consolidation as a downstream activity, BlackLine brings the two processes together. Finance teams gain better visibility and fewer manual handoffs as they move from financial data to consolidated results. This integrated approach can also help finance leaders access trusted financial information sooner, supporting more timely reporting and business decisions. It’s an important step toward a more unified Record-to-Report experience.


## Putting Verity AI to Work Across the Close


We’re also expanding the role of[Verity AI](https://www.blackline.com/products/verity-ai/) across[reconciliation](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/account-reconciliations/)


workflows. Agentic Reconciliations support more intelligent execution of reconciliation activities based on established criteria and controls. Verity™ Score assesses reconciliation quality to highlight exactly where review may be needed. Verity™ Retrieve surfaces relevant financial information, reducing the manual effort required to locate supporting documentation. Together, these capabilities move finance teams toward a touchless close. Routine work is handled more intelligently, freeing people to focus on exceptions and higher-value decisions.


## Bringing More Intelligence to Transaction Matching


With[Verity™ Match](https://www.blackline.com/products/financial-close/transaction-matching/) , BlackLine extends AI-powered intelligence into transaction matching. For organizations with high transaction volumes, matching can require substantial effort to investigate discrepancies and resolve exceptions. Verity Match is designed to reduce that manual intervention so teams can concentrate on the transactions that genuinely require attention. The broader opportunity is to accelerate processing while maintaining confidence in the accuracy and integrity of financial information.


## Connecting the Invoice-to-Cash Lifecycle to Improve Cash Flow


While financial close is a natural starting point for agentic transformation, the opportunity extends across the broader Office of the CFO.[Invoice-to-Cash software](https://www.blackline.com/products/invoice-to-cash/) is another critical area where disconnected processes create friction and delay key decisions. That friction can weaken working capital performance and slow an organization’s response to business opportunities.


Consider the lifecycle of a customer account. Before a sale is completed, finance teams need to assess creditworthiness and manage exposure. Once the customer is onboarded, the work shifts to billing and collections. Remittances must be processed, and any disputes or deductions resolved. When these activities operate in silos, teams may lack the visibility and context needed to act in time. At BeyondTheBlack, we highlighted how BlackLine is expanding its Invoice-to-Cash capabilities to connect more of this lifecycle.


## Building on Verity™ Collect and Verity™ Remit


Verity Collect helps collections teams prioritize activities and focus where they can have the greatest impact. In early trials, Verity Collect reduced human call time by 99%, compressing 45 hours of manual outreach into 30 minutes. Verity Remit brings AI to remittance processing, raising the auto-processing rate from 41% to 73% and achieving a 92% straight-through processing rate on genuine remittances. Together, they provide a foundation for expanding intelligence across additional receivables processes.


## Extending Intelligence Across the Customer Financial Lifecycle


BlackLine also introduced innovations across several additional areas:


-


**Credit & Risk Management:** Helping organizations assess credit exposure and spot emerging risks to make better-informed decisions.


-


**Customer Onboarding:** Simplifying how information is collected and validated to accelerate onboarding.


-


**Disputes & Deductions:** Helping finance teams resolve disputes more efficiently while reducing friction across the receivables lifecycle.


-


**Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) Agent:** Analyzing receivables information to identify opportunities to accelerate collections and recommend actions that improve cash flow.


Individually, these capabilities address important challenges across receivables operations. Collectively, they advance a broader vision: a connected Invoice-to-Cash lifecycle where financial information and intelligence inform decisions across processes rather than remaining confined to individual applications. For finance leaders, that means managing working capital more proactively and responding faster to changing customer needs, with less manual effort along the way.


## What These Innovations Mean for Finance Leaders


Across all three areas of innovation, a common theme emerged at BeyondTheBlack. The next phase of finance transformation creates an operating model where financial data and intelligent agents collaborate directly within a trusted, governed environment.


The business value depends on that trust. When finance teams can confidently rely on AI-generated information and outcomes, they can spend less time validating routine work. That time goes instead to acting on insights and anticipating risks.


For[organizations already using BlackLine](https://www.blackline.com/customers/) , these innovations extend the value of existing investments. They can introduce agentic capabilities gradually while keeping confidence in the numbers. For organizations beginning their transformation journey, they demonstrate the importance of a foundation that supports both today’s automation requirements and tomorrow’s digital workforce. And for finance professionals, they point toward a different way of working: less time managing routine execution and more time applying judgment to move the business forward.


## The Future of Finance Is Coming Into Focus


BeyondTheBlack 2026 offered a glimpse of what becomes possible when intelligent agents and purpose-built financial solutions come together under enterprise-grade governance. From AI-native consolidation and a more touchless close to connected receivables operations and an open, agent-ready platform, the innovations we unveiled represent a significant advancement toward the future of finance.


But this is ultimately about more than technology. It’s about giving finance teams the confidence to put AI to work across increasingly complex processes without losing the control that defines trusted financial operations. And it’s about enabling the Office of the CFO to move beyond managing the work of finance to directing outcomes that drive the business forward.


That is what BeyondTheBlack Orlando announced—and it is what BlackLine is building. As we continue to execute against this platform vision, expect more updates in the months ahead.
